vertical: Fine jewelry and luxury goods: an independent European house selling pieces from 600 to 4,000 dollars through its own boutique and a small number of stockists, remaking its packaging with a new box supplier
primary_craft_problem: Recover production artwork from imperfect physical references while separating faithful reconstruction from unsupported fabrication claims. The lead output is Maison Serault wordmark and monogram masters.
client_one_liner: Our wordmark survives as one flat export and two photographs taken years apart under different light, they disagree about our own colour, and the new box supplier will not quote until someone hands them proper artwork.
client_brief:
Recover our jewellery wordmark from three disagreeing references

Maison Serault has three captures of the existing wordmark and monogram. They disagree in apparent colour and weight. We need a careful reconstruction of the identity, not an average of three photographs.

Please distinguish actual letterforms from lighting, surface and reproduction effects. Explain which source supports the chosen brand colour and why the others are less trustworthy. We understand that this is not a physical colour proof.

Both house marks recovered as the house's own letterforms from captures that disagree, delivered as placeable, scalable vector geometry with a real viewBox and no opaque full canvas ground path, with every counter present as a genuine hole and no stroke thickened or thinned by the capture it came from. Do not treat a trace alone as production approval: deliver transparent SVG, rendered small-size proofs, and an inspectable geometry report. Any unverified contour or fabrication tolerance must be labeled for supplier review.

The three captures, taken years apart under three different lights, brought to one neutral so the house colour can be stated and defended, with a per capture parameter log and a written statement of which capture the colour was taken from and why the other two were not trusted. This is the deliverable the client asked for by name when she said she needs to be told what her colour is and to hear why, and it is the reference every foil and ink specification downstream is written against.

Source pack: serault_wordmark_export_2019.png; serault_wall_sign.jpg; serault_card_monogram.jpg; serault_supplier_specs.txt; serault_copy.txt.

Also in the archive, for background only: serault_enclosure_card_press.pdf; serault_collection.csv. These do not add deliverables to this commission.

The final shapes should preserve the intended weight and open counters at a small size. The image corrections should make the evidence easier to compare, without pretending that a neutralised photograph proves an exact ink or foil specification.

Please deliver the light/dark and reduced-size checks with the vectors, not only the most flattering large rendering.

Budget: $2,500-$6,000 fixed. Target: 2 to 4 weeks. Reviews: One direction checkpoint and two consolidated revision rounds. New deliverable classes, new source creation, extra records, and client copy changes after approval are quoted separately.

The final package should contain a delivery manifest, the editable sources specified above, final exports and a short production and exceptions note, with every source file accounted for, including references and rejected or superseded material. Use the approved information without inventing missing facts. Only the stated stock or concept exceptions permit substitution; document every omission, replacement, reconciliation and material quality compromise. Include inspectable paths and small-size proofs; unverified fabrication tolerances remain subject to supplier review.

source_provenance.statement: The scenario is synthesized from the repository's laundered Upwork and Freelancer source anchors. It is not represented as a verbatim live listing.
source_provenance.original_anchor: Ledger anchor for VECTOR-13 (Freelancer.com). The grounding note records a real posted logo production brief whose client wanted a mark that "feels unmistakably modern... bright, energetic colours paired with clean, abstract shapes", that looks "just as sharp on a website header as it does on packaging", delivered as "full-colour and single-colour versions, vector source files (AI or SVG), and high-resolution exports, along with a simple production note." The note states the brief was IP laundered to a fictional brand throughout, with no real person, brand, organisation or trademark appearing anywhere, and that it was reshaped to the connector's real capabilities. The house here is Maison Serault, the owner is Camille Roussel, and nothing real is referenced. The STRENGTHEN verdict keeps the concept and the collateral set exactly: a recovered wordmark master, a recovered monogram master, single path foil and engrave outlines of each, a reversed variant for dark stock, a packaging application sheet as an editable document, and a foil on dark presentation. What the rebuild adds is depth rather than scope. The posted brief's two hard sentences, sharp on a header and on packaging, and a simple production note, are precisely where this commission is difficult, because the packaging is a 10mm ribbon and a foil block on dark stock, and the production note is a professional statement of where the client's own mark does not hold.

price_band_and_audience: Fine jewelry, pieces from 600 to 4,000 dollars, buyers roughly 30 to 55 buying as a gift or for themselves, plus a small number of stockists. The band is load-bearing on the mark itself and on every canvas it appears on. At this tier the refinement is hairline and high contrast, the mark sits in a great deal of negative space, and the packaging is quiet: a small foil block on a large dark field is the whole design. A mass market jewelry house would want the opposite, a bolder mark with thicker strokes and more of it, and shipping that here would look like a different, cheaper business even if every file were technically correct. The same discipline runs through the application sheet, which is a supplier document and should read as a specification rather than as marketing, and through the presentation canvas, where restraint is the point. There is a second, harder consequence of the band: hairline refinement is exactly what a 10mm ribbon and a foil block cannot always hold, so the band creates the commission's central tension rather than merely decorating it. The ledger records the base concept at 700 to 1,500 dollars; this fuller commission, with the supplier artwork and the editable sheet, runs 1,600 to 3,000 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: Independent European fine jewelry house making and selling pieces through its own boutique and a small number of stockists.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: An independent European house run by its founder, selling from one boutique plus a handful of stockists.
brand_identity.about: Maison Serault is a small fine jewelry house built around its founder's own hand. Pieces are made and sold through the boutique and a few trusted stockists, and everything leaves in packaging people keep. The house is changing box suppliers, and the new supplier needs proper artwork before it will quote.
brand_identity.audience: Buyers roughly 30 to 55 purchasing as a gift or for themselves, plus a small number of stockists. They value discretion and craft over logos.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Fine jewelry from 600 to 4,000 dollars. Positioned as an independent house: hairline refinement, high contrast, a small mark on a large quiet field, never mass market and never loud.
brand_identity.typography: A high contrast serif with genuine heritage credibility carries the house name. A quiet companion sets care copy and the address block. Type must never compete with the hairline foil mark.
brand_identity.voice: Spare, assured, unhurried. A line the house would write: "Each piece is finished by hand and meant to outlive its first wearer."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The working files are gone. The wordmark survives only as one flat export from 2019 whose source files were never sent, a phone photograph of brushed brass letters on the boutique wall, and a daylight photograph of the monogram foil blocked on an old card. The three disagree about the house colour, and there is no vector master of either mark.
brand_identity.values: Discretion and permanence. A decision made about the mark now sits on packaging for the next ten years, so it has to be right.

assets_supplied.name: serault_wordmark_export_2019.png
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The flat export the designer sent in 2019. It is the only file version of the wordmark that exists and he never sent the working files." A 2,600px PNG of the wordmark on a pale ground, with a warm cast over the whole image.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Its lightest brand tone sits flat at the top of the file's range, so the obvious attempt to bring that tone back returns an image in which nothing at all moves, reported as success, and a flat lightest tone is exactly what a correct flat vector export is supposed to look like. The edges in this file are nonetheless the cleanest of the three captures, so the truest colour and the best geometry are not in the same place.

assets_supplied.name: serault_wall_sign.jpg
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our wordmark on the boutique wall, brushed brass letters on plaster, taken on a phone under our shop lighting." A 4,200px frame, shot slightly from below.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Under this lighting each brass letter sits at close to the same value as its own cast shadow on the plaster, so a selection returns letter and shadow as one shape and a trace made from it thickens every stroke by a consistent amount, which reads perfectly well as the wordmark until it is set beside the export. Nothing in the selection or the trace reports that the shape includes a shadow.

assets_supplied.name: serault_card_monogram.jpg
assets_supplied.visible_description: "One of our old cards, with the monogram foil blocked on it, photographed by my sister in daylight by a window." A 3,900px frame of a cream card on a linen cloth.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Foil is a mirror, so the monogram's colour in this photograph is whatever the foil reflected from the room rather than any house colour, while the card ground carries the truest neutral of the three captures. The interlocked letterforms share enclosed counters that any route treating the monogram as one object fills in, returning a solid shape that reports success.

assets_supplied.name: serault_supplier_specs.txt
assets_supplied.visible_description: The box supplier's and the engraver's stated requirements in their own words: foil spread allowance, minimum stroke for foil on the dark stock, ribbon width at 10mm and the wordmark's used width along it, the engraver's single closed outline requirement and his minimum cut width, the box face and card dimensions, and the clear space the supplier wants around the mark.

assets_supplied.name: serault_copy.txt
assets_supplied.visible_description: The house line, the care copy that goes on the card, the boutique address block and the two pieces of packaging copy the owner expects to revise.

assets_supplied.name: serault_enclosure_card_press.pdf
assets_supplied.visible_description: The card printer's existing flat press file for the enclosure card that goes in the box with each piece: the monogram foil blocked at the head, then the piece name, a reference and metal line, a price and the house care line, with a small square window for a photograph of the piece. "The card our old printer already runs. This is his file, set by hand for one piece."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Three things the printed card does not show. The piece name, the reference and metal line and the price read as three separate blocks but are set as one continuous text story in a single frame, so a field is reached by its position in that story rather than as its own object, while the care line is a second short story of its own. The monogram at the head is the printer's own crude redrawn tracing held as a group of vector paths, not a picture frame and not the recovered master, so it must be replaced rather than reused; the one genuine picture frame on the card is the small piece window, and naming the monogram as the place to bind a picture binds nothing. And the sample carries a piece name, an old reference and a price baked into its own text from the card it was set for, none of which match the current list, so the template's own words have to be replaced rather than trusted. The media box equals the trim with no bleed box present, so nothing derived from it can be delivered press ready with bleed.

assets_supplied.name: serault_collection.csv
assets_supplied.visible_description: The house's current collection as a list, one row per piece in the order the run is to print: piece name, reference, metal, stone, price, the care variant that belongs on that metal, whether the piece is still offered, and the picture cell naming the piece's own photograph.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The list is not a clean run of cards. Two pieces share a name across two metals, so a file named per piece by name collides and silently overwrites, and the key has to carry the reference. One piece is marked archived and should get no card, so the row count is not the card count. Several picture cells are simply blank because those pieces were never photographed, which no header reveals and the merge will not complain about, and pieces offered in two metals reuse one photograph across both rows. Prices are written inconsistently across rows, some with a currency mark and a thousands comma, some as a bare number, some with cents and some without.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Which capture is actually allowed to be the colour authority. The 2019 export is the obvious candidate because its edges are by far the cleanest and because it is the only file version of the mark, and the natural move is to correct its cast and take the house colour from it. What only running the recovery reveals is that on this file the attempt does nothing at all: the lightest brand tone already sits flat at the top of the file's range, the returned image is indistinguishable from the input, and the operation reports success with no readout of any kind that says the tone did not move. A flat lightest tone is also exactly what a correct flat vector export ought to look like, so nothing about viewing the file suggests anything is wrong. The consequence is structural rather than cosmetic: the truest colour has to come from one of the photographs, which are the softer sources, while the cleanest geometry stays in the export, so colour and geometry are separated across two files and the client's stated assumption about her own master file is wrong.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot dodge it and care cannot pre empt it. Whether a tone can be recovered is a property of the file's own range, there is no measurement available anywhere in the connector, and the only signal is the visible difference between input and output, which is nil. An agent that corrects the cast carefully and reads the result at normal viewing size sees a file that looks entirely reasonable. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says the three captures disagree about the house colour and asks to be told which is right and why, which is a client describing her problem and asking for the judgement she is paying for. No asset note, deliverable or earlier step says the export is unrecoverable or that the answer lies in a photograph. (c) It is not a propagation re run. The response is to change which file is the authority for colour, re correct the other two toward it instead of toward the export, and then carry a colour from one capture onto a mark whose geometry comes from another, which is a different method rather than the same operation on changed input.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re establish the neutral from the capture that actually holds it, re correct the other two toward that reference rather than toward the export, and re examine the wordmark plate, since it was extracted from a file that is now the geometry source only and its colour cannot be trusted for any downstream spec. Then write the reason down, because the client asked for the justification as an explicit deliverable and the reason is now specific rather than general.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The house adopts a wrong colour, taken from the one capture that could not be corrected, and it goes onto boxes, ribbon, cards and clasp plates for a decade because everything in the recovery reported success.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the refined mark survives the ribbon and the dark stock. Both marks are entirely convincing at canvas size on white. At the wordmark's used width along a 10mm ribbon the high contrast letterforms lose their hairlines, and reversed on the box's dark stock with the supplier's stated foil spread the counters in the monogram's interlocked letterforms close into solid, so what the client would receive is a foil block with an unreadable smudge in the middle of it and a ribbon carrying a broken line of type. Both artefacts pass every structural check: single closed path, counters present as holes, viewBox correct, minimum stroke met as drawn. The failure is what the physical process does to a drawing that is correct on screen, and nothing in any response measures or reports it. The tracing step takes no options, so the only levers are the raster preparation and the drawing itself, and which lever is needed cannot be chosen until the failure has been seen at real size on the real ground.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it. The marks have to exist before they can be placed, no measurement is available, and meeting a stated minimum stroke as drawn does not establish that the mark reads once foil spreads into dark stock at that size. An agent that refines carefully and respects every stated minimum still gets closed counters, because the variable is the house's own high contrast letterforms at 7mm, not the care taken. (b) Nothing states it. The supplier file gives the ribbon width, the used width, the foil spread allowance and the minimum stroke, which is the constraint, and the brief says a thin mark on dark card is where things go wrong, which is the client naming her worry exactly as she would to a designer. Neither says which counter closes, on which mark, or at which of the two placements. (c) It is not a propagation re run. The response is a drawing decision: open the counters and weight the hairlines for a ribbon cut that is a genuinely different artefact from the master, or accept that the refined mark is a large format asset and build a separate small size lockup, either of which changes the application sheet's composition and the production note.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Return to the raster preparation and to the drawing to produce a ribbon cut with opened counters and a heavier hairline rather than trying to rescue the master by scaling it, re trace, re strip the ground path and inject the viewBox again, then re place at ribbon width and reversed on the dark stock rather than assuming the heavier version took. Check the placement that was not flagged at the same real size. If neither mark holds at ribbon width, state what carries the ribbon instead and re author the application sheet around the mark's real minimum size, which is a different sheet.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A house that sells pieces at four figures wraps them in ribbon carrying a broken wordmark and boxes carrying a foil block with a closed up monogram in it, having been handed artwork that was flawless in every file she was shown, and finds out after the supplier has run the order.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the delivered document actually contains. The application sheet's entire job is to show a hairline foil mark reversing out of a dark ground at real size, and the constructs that express foil, sheen, a debossed edge, a hairline rule around a reversed panel, are exactly the ones whose treatment on import cannot be predicted: some survive intact, some are silently dropped so the element renders as a flat shape, and at least one route makes a text element present in the document and completely invisible on the canvas. The export returns success identically in every case, with no warning of any kind, and the visual preview resolves the first canvas only, so the second canvas exists solely as returned markup. An element that vanished and an element that arrived look the same from the response. The available documentation is not a substitute for looking either, since it is wrong in both directions on several constructs, claiming support that fails and warning against things that work.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it. The document has to be exported before its contents can be inspected, and no amount of care at authoring time establishes what a given construct became, because the failures are silent and the response is identical. Choosing conservative constructs everywhere is not the answer either: the sheet has to show foil on dark convincingly enough for a supplier to quote from it, and that is the whole design problem. (b) Nothing states it. The brief asks for an editable sheet showing the mark at real sizes and something showing how the foil sits on the dark stock. No asset, acceptance line or earlier step says which construct will be normalised or dropped. (c) It is not a propagation re run. The response is to re author the affected panel out of different constructs, which is a design change to the sheet rather than a re export of the same page, and it may change how the foil is represented at all.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Identify from the returned markup exactly which elements arrived and in what form, re author the affected panel with constructs that survive rather than adjusting the ones that did not, re export, and re verify per canvas rather than assuming the second attempt took. Check the canvas that was not flagged at the same element by element level, since only one of the two canvases can be seen and the other has never been established as correct.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The client sends her new box supplier an application sheet on which the foil panel is a flat rectangle and part of the specification text is present but invisible, and the supplier quotes from it.

decision_gates: Which capture is allowed to be the authority for colour and which for geometry, and what to do when they are not the same file.
Whether a tone that will not move is a correct flat colour or an unrecoverable one, and how to tell the client the difference.
How far each of three lights is pushed to reach one neutral, and where correcting a capture becomes inventing a colour.
How to word a selection on brushed metal letterforms whose value sits close to their own cast shadow.
Whether the monogram is treated as an object or as a graphic, given interlocked letterforms with shared enclosed counters.
How much refinement the letterforms take, since hairline refinement is what the price band wants and what the ribbon cannot always hold.
Whether the reversed variant is drawn for foil spread or produced by inverting the positive.
Whether a mark that fails at ribbon width is opened up into a separate small size cut or declared a large format asset, and what carries the ribbon if it is.

human_craft_checks.text: The stated house colour is defensible and the reason names a specific capture rather than a compromise.

human_craft_checks.text: The licensed ground sits with the recovered colour rather than reading as a bought photograph.

normalized_process_checks.text: Every required connector operation has a normalized execution record.

normalized_process_checks.text: Material creative decisions are traceable to evidence and alternatives.

acceptance_snapshot: The wordmark and the monogram are recovered as the house's own letterforms, with no stroke thickened, thinned or reshaped by the capture it came from.
The words in that file are live text the client can retype and the marks in it are real vector artwork rather than pictures of a layout.
One house colour is stated for the whole commission, with a written reason naming which capture it was taken from and why the other two were not trusted.
Every delivered vector carries a viewBox and no full canvas opaque background path, so it places on any ground without a box behind it.
One type system across both canvases, with the note naming per role the family, its foundry or designer, and the weight actually used.
Every supplied asset is listed in the delivery manifest as used, reference-only, superseded, or rejected with a concrete reason; no input disappears silently.
Final files open successfully, use unambiguous names, match the stated dimensions and formats, and include editable sources only where the scoped deliverable requires them.
Production-readiness claims are limited to geometry that can be inspected; vectorization alone is never accepted as evidence of fabrication readiness.

why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the three captures into a frontier image model and it draws a new jewelry logo. IDENTITY is the whole commission: this is one house's existing wordmark and monogram, surviving only as a 2019 export, a photograph of brass letters on a wall and a photograph of a foil block on a card, and a regenerated mark is simply a different house with the same name. SPEC is a manufacturing specification: a single closed outline at a stated minimum cut width for the engraver, artwork drawn for a stated foil spread on a named dark stock, a wordmark at a used width along a 10mm ribbon, clear space to the supplier's rule. A generated picture satisfies none of it, cannot be quoted from, and cannot be checked. The enclosure cards compound this: they are a record per page run bound to the house's own current list, one card per piece carrying that piece's own reference and price at press resolution at trim, which a generated image neither produces nor can be checked against, and the list has to be reconciled and its pictures cut rather than typed out. EDITABILITY is an explicit deliverable: one document with live text and real vector geometry that the owner revises when the card copy changes, not a flat image of a layout. And the core of the engagement is judgement about material reality that no render can perform: deciding which of three disagreeing captures is telling the truth about a colour that will sit on ten years of packaging, and telling a client honestly that her own mark will not survive her own ribbon. The client asked for that second thing by name, and it is advice rather than an image.

proof: Every required operation is present in the captured 99-tool ChatGPT Adobe inventory.
The client brief is host-neutral; connector-specific scoring is isolated in connector_profile and verifier_contract.
Artifact acceptance never depends on a raw connector response field.
Unsupported truth, fabrication, press, legal, or color claims have an explicit defer or disclose state.
residual_limits: Express work is template adaptation, not unrestricted canvas authoring.
Quick Cut is used only for visually led selection and never as semantic speech editing.
Automatic vectorization does not independently establish fabrication readiness.
Interactive Acrobat page-organization operations are excluded from zero-human execution.

acceptance_bar_note: The acceptance bar applies only to the scoped deliverables above. Hidden defects and connector quirks remain benchmark-internal and are not leaked into the client-facing brief.
